Discover Our Junior Schools
Welcome to Senior School
Welcome to Sixth Form
Welcome to Alleyn's Junior School
We trust that this website will offer you a glimpse of the life and character of the Junior School. At the heart of our school community are the children, from Reception to Year 6, who flourish within an avowedly co-educational and academically selective setting.
Head's Welcome
Glorious grounds and fantastic facilities
The Junior School is an intimate and friendly community based in a modern building specially designed for the all-rounded, nurturing education we offer, and nestled in a 28 acre site with glorious grounds and fantastic sporting facilities.
Explore our Junior School facilities
Celebrate your ideas
Here at our school, there is always something going on, where the passion of our staff and the ideas of our young pupils are encouraged and celebrated. Our values ‘Respect, Opportunity, Courage, Curiosity and Kindness' are the cornerstone of our school and pervade all aspects of our outstanding curriculum and co-curriculum.
Read more about our values
Academic curiosity is constantly nurtured throughout the classrooms from the earliest age, with committed and passionate teachers, and an inspiring and wide-ranging curriculum which leads to our children achieving excellent results in external competitions, poetry and story writing, general knowledge and science quizzes, language, maths and memory challenges.

Be kind to your world
‘Respect’ for the environment is also taught from an early age as we want to teach our pupils to be ‘Kind’ to their world. Following long-running encouragement promoting sustainable modes of transport, we are proud to have seen a significant increase in the number of families coming by foot, cycle, or scooter. Children also engage in a variety of ‘green initiatives’ around the school, often through the Eco-Council.
Respect and kindness for one another are two of our key values, and which we promote daily in our school. We believe our four vertical houses embed friendships and profound loyalty to one another during the course of every child’s time from Reception to Year 6. Each form group is suitably intimate yet a healthy size, with a very equal gender split. This size and the fact that we have both Infants and Juniors together under one roof, nurture an intimacy, a togetherness, a support for each other and a sense of belonging and knowing that you can be recognised and known by your peers and all the staff. You will find that everyone looks out for one another and is kind to each other.
Excel in your passions
Our children are more than just strong performers on the academic front. We offer a plethora of opportunities for your children to explore their passions and interests, as a well-rounded education is important to us. We live this value through the range of visiting speakers, numerous themed days, exciting day and residential trips and over 100 clubs each term. Indeed, if your children attend our school, do not be surprised if they develop a proclivity for music, become thespians or start to excel in sports!
Explore Co-Curricular Opportunities
Pastoral care and safeguarding are central to every single thing that happens every day and given the highest priority as we want the children to feel and be safe. Our pastoral framework gives them the space and the confidence to be the best versions of themselves. We are proud to have children come to our school from a variety of family backgrounds with different interests and characters and to give them the endless courage to express their interests, dreams, and desires. Our community is very diverse racially and culturally and we celebrate such differences through our curriculum, assemblies and host of special events.
An inclusive learning environment
We are a proud co-educational school. We recognise that there are differences, as well as many similarities, between boys and girls and so we make sure that we offer a curriculum and co-curriculum that is very broad and caters for the needs of all children, without assuming that they all learn in one way or another because of that gender.
We believe that a coeducational environment contributes significantly in enabling children to be at ease with themselves and discovering different qualities within their own character as well as being prepared for the realities of life outside school.
We would love to welcome you to our school to learn more. Please do not hesitate to register for any of our open days to see the school in person and ask any questions you may have.
Simon Severino Head of Alleyn's Junior School

Welcome to Alleyn's Oakfield
Alleyn's Oakfield became part of Alleyn's School from September 2025. Whether your child starts their Alleyn's junior school journey at Alleyn's Junior School or Alleyn's Oakfield they will experience the same commitment to excellence, care and opportunity, with the added confidence of an assured place at Alleyn’s Senior School.
Head's Welcome
I am delighted to be joining Alleyn’s Oakfield at an exceptionally exciting time in the school’s history, as we continue to grow and thrive as a part of the Alleyn’s family. The excitement is palpable when you talk to the engaging, confident and fun-loving children who walk through the gates each morning.
Pete Whitmell Alleyn's Oakfield
Alleyn’s Oakfield is a place where children can be themselves and find their passions – both academically and outside the classroom – with the support of an outstanding team throughout their journey.
Our lessons are designed with "wow" moments in mind, balancing academic rigour with creativity, exploration and discovery. We want children to be excited by learning, ask great questions and develop a genuine love of finding things out. Our dedicated staff are testament to the commitment and love of learning that unites our school community, where every effort is made to ensure that children can become All They Can Be.
Oakfield has a rich and interesting history, having provided an exceptional education to generations of young learners for the last 140 years. Children at Alleyn's Oakfield benefit from the warmth and individual attention of a nurturing junior school setting as well as the ambition, expertise and opportunity that come from being part of – and going on to - one of London's leading schools: Alleyn’s School.
We are firm believers that education is a collaboration and we love having parents on site, sharing in the life of the school and seeing what goes on each day. Please do take the opportunity to come and visit us – I know you will feel an unmistakeable buzz which is a certain sign that outstanding primary education is occurring all around you!
Another Place to Grow
Learning here is rooted in curiosity and creativity, both in and beyond the classroom. Whether it’s through music, sport, drama or outdoor learning, children are given the space and support to discover their passions and develop their voice.
Explore our curriculum
Alleyn’s Oakfield is a place alive with energy, warmth and ambition. Every day, our pupils are encouraged to explore new ideas, take meaningful risks, and build lasting relationships within a nurturing environment.
Find Your Thing
We believe a great education goes beyond the classroom. At Alleyn’s Oakfield, pupils can explore their passions through a rich programme of trips, themed days, visiting speakers and over 50 clubs. Whether discovering a love of music, drama or sport, every child is encouraged to find their thing.
Explore co-curricular opportunities
A Proud Heritage, A Modern Future
We want our spaces to make children feel energised, engaged, and supported throughout the school day.
For more than 140 years, Oakfield has educated generations of young learners. Today, as part of the Alleyn’s family, we are carefully modernising our classrooms to support contemporary learning, while respecting the character and architecture of our historic setting.
We look forward to showing you and your family around.
Joining Alleyn's Oakfield
Join us for our next Open Morning. Come and discover what makes Alleyn’s Oakfield so special and meet the team behind Alleyn’s Oakfield. Please book a space using the form below. We look forward to meeting you.
There are occasional vacancies in some year groups at Alleyn's Oakfield.

pageCache.text:

Welcome from the Head
There is a magical ‘all’ in Alleyn’s, which explains the warm sense of welcome you feel upon stepping through our gates.
At Alleyn’s, we pride ourselves on having a wonderful community of bright, happy, and engaged pupils who make our school the special place that it is. Our teaching staff are passionate experts in their fields, and they care deeply about their mission to educate and support our pupils, providing inspiration and guidance in whatever path they choose to take.
Alleyn’s is a school rooted in 400 years of history, but we have always had a forward-thinking lens to the future. We believe in embracing new technologies and equipping our pupils with a strong core of skills for tomorrow so that they can be confident and engaged citizens of the modern world.
Individuality is celebrated at Alleyn’s. Pupils are encouraged to be exactly who they are, on their journey to becoming all they can be. Fuelled by the nurture of their self-expression, our young people are fun, and they are funny, quirky, intelligent, kind, and well-rounded. They are encouraged to look up and out, and always outside the box.
There are many reasons I am so proud to be the Head of this special school, from the outstanding academic results, sporting triumphs, and performance talent, but the people make our school what it is. Community sits at the very heart of an Alleyn’s education, embodied by our outreach work, partnerships, or volunteering; our pupils care about each other, they care about the world, and they care about their place in it.
Opening the hearts and minds of our pupils
When children are happy, they do well. While we are very proud of the truly outstanding results that our pupils achieve, rather like the original Renaissance scholars, we see exam results as a by-product of the education we offer, not the central goal. Instead, we seek to open the hearts and minds of our pupils. We encourage them to approach the acquisition of knowledge as a great adventure; to be generous and reflective in their study and to recognise that learning doesn't stop when you leave the classroom, or even when you leave the school.
Our ROCCK values (Respect, Opportunity, Curiosity, Courage and Kindness) are strong golden threads that run through school life, and we are wholeheartedly committed to making an Alleyn’s education accessible to talented children of all backgrounds, with a generous bursary scheme to support this.
If Alleyn’s sounds like a place for your child to flourish, I’d be delighted to welcome you into our school for a tour and to give you a sense of what makes it so special.
Jane was the recipient of the Tatler Schools “Best Head of an Independent School” award.

Welcome to Sixth Form
Alleyn’s Sixth Form has a distinct identity and feel, creating a genuine sense of moving up to something new and exciting, even if students are coming from our own Year 11 - and almost all of our Year 11 students do stay on for Sixth Form.
Each September, we welcome roughly 40 new students from a wide range of schools and backgrounds to join our current Year 11 pupils when they start Upper School. We mix up the tutor groups purposefully to ensure new arrivals integrate easily, and they’ll also be assigned to a House, where they can get to know younger year groups as well.
The teachers know the students well: they know their strengths, and how to nurture their future success at A level and beyond. We expand our year group slightly and take on more students at 16+, some of whom join with a means-tested bursary. We are lucky to attract high-quality 16+ applicants, many of whom come to us seeking the co-educational experience that we can offer.
As well as the academic curriculum, our Sixth Formers take on many leadership responsibilities. As Senior Prefects, they play a key role in leading school duties as well as performing an important public-facing role at open days and interview days. Sixth Formers who are Lower School prefects lead activities for Year 7 and Year 8 pupils during their tutor time and students also have many opportunities to take responsibility within the co-curriculum, in the CCF, Duke of Edinburgh's Award Scheme, Sport, Theatre, Music or Volunteering.
Our Sixth Form provides a real opportunity for students to flourish, which is our ultimate aim for them. The sense of developing their individual identity permeates the whole of Sixth Form life at Alleyn's, helping the students to be fully prepared for life beyond School.
Ms Alex Smith Head of Sixth Form

Community and Partnerships
We believe that an education is about more than what happens in the classroom. It's also about the difference our pupils make in the world around them. From their very first years with us, children learn that they belong to a wider community, and that they have the power and responsibility to give something back.
Giving back, at every age
Charitable giving runs through the life of the school, from our youngest junior pupils to our senior students. Our Junior School enjoys successful relationships with a wide range of local and national charities and community organisations, including The Norwood and Brixton Food Bank, Link Age, The Royal British Legion, Children in Need, Save the Children and Macmillan Cancer Support. Each year, our Year Six Charity Monitors carefully select a local charity to support throughout the school year. Past choices have included the Denmark Hill Adventure Playground and the London Community Boxing gym in Peckham. A weekly tuck shop, termly charity breakfasts, discos, movie nights and many more child-inspired events all help raise money and awareness for the chosen cause, and teach our pupils early on what it means to care about the world beyond the classroom.
As pupils move up through the school, they take on more responsibility, with senior students leading their own campaigns, choosing charities to support, and organising events that bring the whole school community together. Our Senior School enjoys successful relationships with a wide range of local charities and community organisations, including The Norwood and Brixton Food Bank, Girls United, King's College Hospital, Get Rid of It Donate, the Lambeth & Southwark Primary Schools Football League, The St Matthew's Project and the Woodcraft Folk youth group. Each year, our pupils, families and staff raise thousands of pounds for local, national and international charities. Along the way, pupils build leadership, teamwork and empathy that stay with them long after they leave.
Learning together
Our commitment to partnership goes further still. Through our Senior School Partnerships Programme, our students and staff work alongside local schools on shared academic, cultural and sporting projects that benefit everyone involved.
Sharing facilities
We are fortunate to have outstanding facilities, and we believe they should serve our wider community too. Throughout the year, we share our sports grounds, swimming pool, theatre, classrooms and other spaces with local state schools, charities and youth organisations. Local primary schools join us each summer to hold their sports days on our fields and track, and our theatre plays host to their end-of-year productions, giving young performers a real stage to shine on. Whether it's a youth group training on our pitches or a local charity hosting an event in our hall, these partnerships create real opportunities and lasting relationships.

Performing Arts Facilities
Alleyn’s offers a range of performance and rehearsal spaces for community and commercial hire; including the RIBA award-winning MCT, the atmospheric Great Hall, and a number of studio spaces.
To enquire about hiring a space with us please contact [email protected].
The MCT is a modern, flexible performance space, usually set up as a medium-scale proscenium house and has a seating capacity of around 344 depending on the set up. There is a lift to the first and second levels and the auditorium has dedicated wheelchair spaces available.
The stage floor is a semi-sprung blonde, European Oak floating composite laminate, a black Harlequin Studio vinyl floor is available is also available.
The stage can be extended with the Forestage, alternatively this can be set up as an orchestra pit. Please note that this would take out the front two rows of seating.
There are two changing rooms and two green rooms located on the group floor, as well as three classrooms on the floor above from additional backstage space.

We also have a performance space with a stage in our Main Building called The Great Hall. The Great Hall can seat up to 350 over two floors depending on the set up of the space. There are plenty of classrooms surrounding the hall that can be used as green rooms or changing rooms.

Senior School Partnerships
Partnership is part of an Alleyn’s education.
At Alleyn’s, we believe education should extend beyond the classroom and beyond the school gates. Through our Partnerships Programme, pupils work alongside local schools, community organisations and young people across Southwark and beyond – sharing experiences, learning from one another and making a meaningful contribution to our local community.
At Alleyn’s we believe that diversity of experience prepares children to go out into the world and make the most of the multitude of opportunities it presents.
Our partnerships programme takes pupils on a voyage of self-discovery through a tailored curriculum designed to build essential life skills alongside confidence and empathy.
Why does this progression matter? Because partnership does more than build communication, empathy, confidence, initiative and leadership. Above all, it helps young people understand that they belong to something larger than themselves.
Partnership, not simply outreach
Our partnerships are built on collaboration and reciprocity.
We work closely with primary and secondary schools, charities and community organisations to understand where we can contribute, while recognising how much our own pupils and staff gain from working alongside others.
That can mean a year 11 Alleyn’s student mentoring a Year 5 mathematician on a Saturday morning; a Year 12 student delivering science, music, drama or sport in a local primary school; pupils from different Southwark schools working together through the Southwark Schools Learning Partnership; or students establishing and leading an initiative that can be shared across the borough.
The activities are diverse, but the principle is consistent: young people working with young people, taking increasing responsibility and discovering what they can contribute.
A school connected to its community
Our partnerships span academic enrichment, sport, music, the arts, volunteering, mentoring, social action, charitable work and the sharing of our facilities and expertise.
Some opportunities are led by staff. Increasingly, others are shaped and led by pupils themselves.
Together they form something bigger than a collection of outreach activities. They are part of our ambition to develop young people who are curious about the world around them, confident working with people different from themselves and prepared to use their skills, energy and influence for the benefit of others.
Participate. Take responsibility. Lead.
That is the journey we want partnership to offer every Alleyn’s pupil.

Staff and Governors
With a shared vision, Alleyn’s staff and governors work together to enable our pupils to become all they can be.
Governors enable our school to run as effectively as possible. They work alongside our senior leaders and support our teachers to provide excellent education to all our pupils. They oversee management decisions including strategy, policy, budgeting and staffing.
If you are looking for an opportunity to join our Board of Governors, we are currently inviting applications. For more information please visit our Join Our Team page. To contact the Clerk to the Governors please email [email protected]
Our governors
The Executive Group
The Executive Group is chaired by our Head Jane Lunnon who is joined by the Head of Alleyn’s Junior School Simon Severino and our Deputy Heads, COO and CFO. This team is further supported by our Senior Leadership Team (SLT) which shares the collective responsibility for all aspects of School leadership and management. Each member is directly accountable to the Head for their area of leadership. Members of the SLT are also assigned specific responsibilities associated with their post.
The Governors of Alleyn’s are keen to identify committed volunteers to join the Governing Board. Led by the Chair of Governors, the Board is responsible for setting the strategic direction of the School, defining the School’s educational and co-curricular offering and ensuring the School’s continued long-term financial stability. The Board works as a team to deliver on the School’s commitment to offer an outstanding holistic education, in a safe and secure environment.
We anticipate that vacancies to join the Governing Board will exist through the next one to four years. With this in mind, we are particularly keen to receive applications from individuals with expertise in the Arts - performing, visual, applied literary, film, studio, curatorial.

The Future of Learning
True to the spirit of our founder, Edward Alleyn, we embrace opportunities to shape the future of our children and their education, so that we as a School can continue to evolve into All We Can Be.
The Future of Learning
We want to be at the vanguard of learning, soaking up new thinking and innovation close to home and across the world. Children can be the freshest thinkers and it is our duty to give them the materials to bring their creativity, sense of wonder and enthusiasm to every day at school, so that they develop a love of learning in its purest sense, as well as build the skills that they will need for the jobs of the future. Grounded in our strong history and the excellent education we offer today, our mission is to shape a future curriculum that combines new thinking and exciting advances in tech with traditional disciplines to prepare children for the world of tomorrow.
Tech innovation
We believe that education and learning sit hand in hand with innovation. We are establishing a global network of partners so that we can collaborate with leading experts to bring new ideas, technologies and disciplines into the global classroom. It is essential to ensure pupils are equipped with the ability to innovate, adapt and think critically using advance digital skills so they can navigate, contribute to and thrive in an ever-evolving, interconnected global digital society. Digital expertise should be integrated into, not separate from, a future-focused, first-rate education and core tenets that underline human creativity, ethics and communication should remain at its core.

Book Here
Unlock your child’s imagination with our fun and engaging art workshops, delivered in partnership with talented artists Dina & Tracy. Each week offers a fresh experience, as children explore different artists, styles, and themes through hands-on activities over the course of two days.
Our workshops are all about creativity, confidence, and connection. Children will make new friends, discover new techniques, and bring home a collection of unique and varied artwork they’ll be proud to share.
Whether your child is a budding artist or just loves to get creative, these sessions are a wonderful way to inspire and nurture their artistic journey in a warm, welcoming environment.
Workshops are available for children in Years 3 to 8 and are open to pupils from all schools, not just those attending Alleyn's.

Higher Education and Careers
Career describes our journey through life, learning and work.
Careers
We need to actively develop our careers to make the best of them. This process of career development takes skill as well as knowledge and the right attitude. Individuals need to work on career development skills throughout their lives.
Career Development Institute (CDI)
At Alleyn’s, we place great emphasis around building excitement about Careers through these three steps:
These stages help to prepare pupils for life after Alleyn’s, to enable them to make well-informed decisions as they embark on next steps towards university and/or apprenticeships, having started to actively consider what is important to them in their bigger picture of life and work in the future.
Alleyn’s pupils are supported as they reflect on their strengths and skills; explore jobs of the future; gain insights about different ways of working such as employment, freelancing and entrepreneurship, build relationships (networking); learn goal setting techniques; undertake work experience; break through stereotypes; learn about personal branding and how positive the purposeful use of social media can be in career development. They will also write CVs; practice interviews; get clear information on multiple routes towards their career goals (including the recognition of portfolio careers) and understand more about how economy, politics and society connect with their own lives and careers.
All pupils at Alleyn’s have access to Unifrog, a universal destinations platform (it is introduced to Year 7s in the summer term) and further information about the careers programme will be published here shortly.
The careers department has been my go to place for university, work experience and career support. It's where I always find valuable advice and have always felt hugely supported. They have been invaluable through my journey for the past few years and the tips and wisdom never fail to amaze and motivate me!
Romy, Year 13 (2021-2022)
The careers provision in PSHE for Year 11 has been really useful and have given a lot of pupils more of a sense of direction, tempered by a reminder to keep an open mind for a wide breadth of career options. This is supplemented by talks and interviews with a wide range of people who are seasoned professionals in their area, and hearing their personal experiences has been extremely helpful.
Hailey, Year 11 (2021-2022)
Alleyn’s School: Provider Access Policy
Donate your time: share your career stories
Career curiosity in the Lower School
Higher education
Each year, the vast majority of our students progress to their first-choice courses at UK and overseas universities or other specialist centres of learning.
Through offering advice and support, information and offering mock exams and interviews we prepare students for life beyond Alleyn’s.
Advice and support
We have a dedicated Higher Education Co-ordinator supporting the team of teachers who provide advice and support on the application process, led by the Director of University Admissions.
Informed decisions
We organise an annual Higher Education Fair for Year 12 students and their parents from Alleyn’s and our partner schools where, this year, over 30 representatives from universities visited us. We also organise specialist talks on applying to Oxford and Cambridge, applying overseas, applying for medicine, or for a degree apprenticeship.
Preparation
Through our Careers Centre, located in the heart of the School, we organise mock interviews for our sixth formers with leading industry professionals as well as workshops on the importance of body language at interview, emotional intelligence and the role of social media in today’s job market.
Our aim is that every student is encouraged to apply for the path that best suits them. For example, aside from UK universities, every year students successfully gain places on prestigious music and drama courses or Foundation Art programmes or choose to study overseas (in Canada and the USA).

Sixth Form: Higher Education and Careers
It is our mission at Alleyn’s to help students ‘find their thing’ whatever that may be, so they leave school confident, excited, and well-equipped for the future.
The majority of our students leave us to go to top universities in the UK and overseas (with 12% going to Oxford or Cambridge and 85% in total going to Russell Group universities) but we help our students to find many other opportunities including degree apprenticeships, Foundation Art courses, or specialist music and drama courses.
We have a dedicated careers team, to guide students on their journey to what they might like to do, and how to get there, whether that is through university or a more vocational pathway.
When it comes to university admissions, we have a dedicated team to support with that too. Our UCAS team will work alongside students as they apply for their top choice universities and support them with all the admin involved. If they are considering an overseas university, there is a team to help with that too.
We run a variety of events throughout the year as well, to open students’ eyes to different career pathways including the Higher Education Fair, Futures Day and the Higher Education Days with a focus on Personal Statement writing and the Alumni Café where Year 12 talk to our alumni about all aspects of university life.
